headline: Highest risk is medium: Pipecat’s shared-bus, networked defaults can cascade or leak when paired with LightZero, but LightZero itself is local-only and non-writing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network ingress, so it cannot ingest Pipecat output by default. Pipecat does have shared-bus session state, but without a bridge from LightZero there is no plausible injection channel in this pair.
conditions: IF LightZero is manually wired to consume Pipecat text from a shared bus or clipboard, reassess upward.
IF an external orchestrator copies Pipecat output into LightZero prompts, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate processes with no shared message bus.
Do not pipe Pipecat transcripts into LightZero inputs.
Disable any manual copy-paste workflow between them during evaluation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress, while Pipecat handles text, audio, video, and can call external APIs. The pair only leaks if sensitive content is introduced into Pipecat and then forwarded elsewhere; LightZero itself is not a leak source.
conditions: IF sensitive text/audio/video is routed into Pipecat and then sent to an allowlisted third-party API, leakage risk increases.
IF LightZero is used to generate content that Pipecat forwards off-box, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or personal data into Pipecat sessions.
Review Pipecat provider allowlists before enabling live traffic.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use the network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with Pipecat. Pipecat’s shared bus is internal coordination, not a conflicting write surface against LightZero.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped with external write permissions or git access, reassess conflict risk.
IF both agents are given the same mutable workspace by an orchestrator, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep Pipecat state in its own process boundary.
Do not mount a shared writable directory unless required.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can treat upstream text as conversation state on a shared bus, so LightZero-generated outputs could be propagated without verification if an orchestrator connects them. LightZero is not authoritative, but Pipecat’s default real-time pipeline makes downstream over-trust plausible.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds LightZero outputs directly into Pipecat prompts or actions, cascading error becomes active.
IF Pipecat is configured to act on model text without validation, severity remains medium or higher.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step between agents.
Tag LightZero outputs as untrusted before Pipecat consumes them.
Limit Pipecat to read-only summarization in the integration.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for LightZero, and Pipecat’s docs-only profile lists broad media handling plus third-party API calls. The pair only raises compliance concerns if regulated data is introduced into Pipecat; LightZero is not a compliance-sensitive processor here.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed by Pipecat providers, compliance review is required.
IF the deployment requires residency guarantees not met by the chosen Pipecat provider, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Select providers with documented residency and retention terms.
Record the data classes allowed in the integration.
